content.user_title: Apply SOLID Principles to Object-Oriented Code
content.value_statement: Object-oriented code becomes difficult to test and extend when responsibilities and dependencies are unclear. This skill provides practical SOLID reviews, examples, and refactoring guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains each SOLID principle with TypeScript examples.
Identifies common design smells linked to individual principles.
Compares problematic designs with more maintainable alternatives.
Suggests focused interfaces, dependency injection, and composition.
Provides a checklist for reviewing object-oriented designs.
limitations: Examples are TypeScript-oriented and may require adaptation for other languages.
The skill provides design guidance, not automated static analysis.
Examples omit production details such as error handling and persistence security.
SOLID recommendations require context and may add unnecessary abstraction to simple code.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Design
use_cases.description: Map classes and interfaces to SOLID principles before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Services
use_cases.description: Find mixed responsibilities, rigid conditionals, and tightly coupled dependencies in existing services.

use_cases.title: Teach Design Principles
use_cases.description: Use concise examples and review questions during mentoring or team workshops.

prompt_templates.title: Explain One Principle
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the {principle} principle using a small example in {language}. Include one violation and one improved design.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Class
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this {class description} for SOLID violations. Name each issue, explain its impact, and suggest focused changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an incremental SOLID refactoring plan for {component}. Preserve behavior, identify tests first, and explain each design tradeoff.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate {architecture description} against all five SOLID principles. Prioritize material risks and avoid abstractions without a current use case.

output_examples.input: Review a user service that creates accounts, sends email, validates input, and generates reports.
output_examples.output: The service violates single responsibility. Separate account creation, validation, email delivery, and reporting, then inject those collaborators into the workflow.

output_examples.input: Assess a payment processor that adds each payment type through another conditional branch.
output_examples.output: The processor resists extension. Define a payment method contract and let each payment type implement processing without changing the coordinator.

output_examples.input: Review a repository that constructs its database client internally.
output_examples.output: The repository depends on a concrete implementation. Inject a database abstraction so tests and alternative providers can supply compatible implementations.

best_practices: Apply SOLID where change, testing, or reuse creates measurable pressure.
Preserve behavior with tests before restructuring responsibilities or dependencies.
Prefer small, domain-focused abstractions with more than one realistic implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not split every method into a separate class.
Do not introduce interfaces only to follow a principle mechanically.
Do not ignore security, performance, or domain constraints during refactoring.

faq.question: Which languages can use this skill?
faq.answer: The principles apply broadly to object-oriented languages, although the included examples use TypeScript.

faq.question: Does the skill modify source files?
faq.answer: It provides analysis and refactoring guidance. File modification depends on the AI tool and the instructions you provide.

faq.question: Should every project apply all five principles?
faq.answer: No. Apply each principle when it reduces current design pressure without adding unjustified complexity.

faq.question: Can it review legacy code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide relevant classes, dependencies, tests, and constraints for a focused review.

faq.question: Does it replace architecture review?
faq.answer: No. It supports design discussion but cannot determine every domain, operational, security, or performance constraint.

faq.question: How should I request a useful refactor?
faq.answer: Include the code context, desired behavior, test coverage, change constraints, and the design problem you observe.
